note: Maps each Afterglow icon id to the ReactOS icon it replaces. status is named when a ReactOS object is named and unmapped otherwise. resource is the module and icon group id to replace (for the Explorer toolbar, the browseui.dll bitmap strips and the cell index); also lists more groups or cells that take the same icon, each with what uses it. A resource is null unless the id is verified, and evidence says how: source (ReactOS 0.4.16 source, tag 0.4.16-release) and binary (the stock 0.4.16 i386 file holds that group). Every null is unverified, not guessed. bitmaps lists the bitmaps the art in desktop/dialogs, desktop/cards (the back, the empty-pile marks and the faces) and the logon bar replaces, by module and bitmap resource id, with the stock size and depth. A group can be a string where the module names it by string (a named resource, not a number). colours lists the colours compiled into code that the art is drawn to match, with where they are.

resource.use: traydeskbtn.cpp loads imageres.dll -110 first and falls back to shell32.dll -35 (IDI_SHELL_DESKTOP, the Desktop folder's icon). ReactOS 0.4.16 ships no imageres.dll, so the button shows the Desktop folder; a resource-only imageres.dll holding group 110 gives it its own icon without touching shell32.dll.
